Harbour CRM uses three terms with specific meanings:
Client: your business, the account that uses Harbour CRM.
Your Client profile holds your Client name, Client contact number and billing details.
Contact: a person your business deals with, such as a customer or a lead.
Company: an organisation your Contacts work for.

Contacts in Harbour CRM: an overview
how do I add a contact
what is a contact in a CRM
A Contact is the heart of Harbour CRM.
It is one of your own customers, kept as a single, tidy record rather than scattered across inboxes, spreadsheets and sticky notes.
Each Contact holds the details you reach for most: a name, a phone number, an email address, a status and free-form notes.
Everything about that person sits in one place, so anyone on your team can pick up a conversation without asking around.
Adding a Contact takes moments, and you can keep adding as your customer base grows.
Contacts can be linked to a Company, attached to Deals, and extended with custom fields for the details that are specific to your business.
Keeping a reliable phone and email list for the whole team
Recording who was spoken to and what was agreed
Grouping people by status so the next follow-up is obvious
Exporting the list when it is needed elsewhere
Harbour CRM is built to be simple to start with and roomy enough to grow into.
Once you're signed in, the help centre walks you through each step.
People change phone numbers, move jobs and switch email addresses.
A CRM is only as useful as the details inside it, so Harbour CRM makes it easy to update a Contact whenever something changes.
A Contact's phone number, email address, status and notes can all be edited on the record itself.
Because each Contact lives in one place, a correction made once is seen by everyone on your team straight away.
There is no second spreadsheet to fix and no old copy lingering in someone's inbox.
Calls and emails reach the right person the first time
Your team spends less time hunting for the latest number
Follow-ups feel considered rather than careless
A simple habit goes a long way.
When a customer mentions a new phone number or email during a conversation, update the Contact while it is fresh, and add a note about what changed if it is worth remembering.
Harbour CRM keeps editing light so that accuracy does not become a chore.

Companies and how Contacts link to them
link a contact to a company
Often several people at the same organisation matter to your business, and Harbour CRM reflects that with Companies.
A Company record holds the details of an organisation: its phone number, website and address.
Contacts can then be linked to the Company they belong to, so you can see at a glance who works where, and who else you know at the same business.
This is useful in a few ways:
A main switchboard number lives on the Company, while direct lines live on each Contact
When someone leaves, the Company and its other Contacts remain intact
Deals can be understood in the context of the organisation behind them
New team members can see the whole relationship, not just one name
A Client who sells to individuals can work happily with Contacts alone, and add Companies later if the business moves towards organisations.
The result is a tidier, more human picture of your customers.

what is a deal in a CRM
A Deal is a piece of potential business: something your business hopes to sell to a Contact or Company.
Harbour CRM lets you record each Deal with a value, so you always know what is on the table.
Deals move through the pipeline, a series of stages that mirror how your sales actually progress.
Seeing every Deal in its stage gives your team a shared picture of where things stand, which conversations need a nudge and which are close to the line.
What the pipeline helps you do:
See what is early, what is advancing and what is nearly done
Spot Deals that have been sitting still for too long
Talk about sales with the same words and the same view
Understand the total value of work in progress
Because Deals connect to Contacts and Companies, the story behind each one is never far away.
Notes, phone numbers and history sit alongside the value and the stage.
It is a clear, calm way to run a sales process without heavy software.

Winning and losing Deals: forecasting the outcome
In Harbour CRM a Deal can be marked as won when the sale is secured, or as lost when it is not going ahead.
If circumstances change, a lost Deal can be reopened and worked again.
Recording outcomes honestly is one of the most valuable habits in sales.
Won Deals show what is working.
Lost Deals, kept on file rather than deleted, show where opportunities slip away and give you something to learn from.
Because each Deal carries a value, your outcomes build a practical picture for forecasting:
What you have won so far
What is still open in the pipeline
What has been lost, and how often
This is not a crystal ball.
It is a grounded view, built from your own records, that helps you plan with more confidence and talk about the next quarter with facts to hand.
Customers who said no last month sometimes say yes later, and having the history intact makes that conversation easier.

Custom fields: make records fit your business
No two businesses keep track of the same things.
A florist might want a delivery preference, an accountant a financial year end, a trainer a course level.
Custom fields let you record exactly the details that matter, right on the record.
Custom fields can be added to records such as Contacts, Companies and Deals.
Once a field exists, it appears alongside the standard details like phone, email and value, and can be filled in for each record as needed.
Referral source, so you know where customers come from
Preferred contact method, such as phone or email
Anything else your team keeps asking about
This keeps Harbour CRM from becoming a place where you squeeze information into the wrong box.
Instead, the CRM adapts to the way your business already works, and the details your team needs sit within easy reach.
Start with the standard fields, then add your own as the need becomes clear.

Search and filters: find the right record fast
As your list of Contacts grows, finding the right person should never feel like a treasure hunt.
Harbour CRM includes search and filters so you can get to the record you need in moments.
Search is for when you know what you are looking for: a name, an email address or part of a phone number.
Filters are for when you want to narrow a longer list, such as every Contact with a particular status.
Finding a customer while they are on the phone
Listing everyone who is waiting on a follow-up
Looking up a Company or a Deal without scrolling
Checking a group of Contacts before an export
Good search also encourages good habits.
When your team trusts that anything can be found quickly, they are more willing to record details as they go, and the CRM becomes more complete and more useful.
It works the same whether you have fifty Contacts or several thousand.

Your Contacts belong to you, and Harbour CRM makes it simple to take a copy whenever you need one.
Contacts can be exported as a CSV file, a plain and widely supported format that opens in common spreadsheet programs.
People export Contacts for many sensible reasons:
Keeping a periodic backup of the customer list
Reviewing or tidying records in a spreadsheet
Sharing a list with an accountant or adviser
Preparing a mail-out or event invitation list
Having peace of mind that the data is always within reach
Because search and filters help you narrow your Contacts first, an export can be as focused as you like, whether that is the whole list or one particular group.
The ability to export is part of how Harbour CRM treats your data: it is yours, and it is never locked away.
Please note that export is available for Contacts, and Harbour CRM does not currently offer an import feature.

add a note to a contact
Who did you speak to last week? What did they ask for? What did you promise? Notes on each Contact give your business a place to capture those details, so nothing depends on one person remembering.
Notes sit on the Contact record, next to the phone number, email address and status.
Anyone on your team who opens the record can see the background and carry on the conversation naturally, which customers notice and appreciate.
Useful things to put in a note:
A summary of a phone call and what was agreed
Personal touches, like a preferred time to ring
Reasons a Deal moved forward or stalled
Reminders about what to follow up on
Over time, notes build into a living history of the relationship.
When a team member goes on leave or moves on, the knowledge stays with the Contact instead of leaving with them.
Keep notes short, factual and kind.
They are a working record, and they make the next conversation easier.

Contact statuses: knowing who needs attention
Not every Contact is in the same place.
Some are brand new, some are in conversation, and some are long-standing customers.
A status on each Contact lets you see that at a glance.
Status is a simple label that sits on the Contact record alongside the phone number, email address and notes.
Because it is easy to change, it can move as the relationship does, from a first enquiry through to an ongoing customer.
Deciding who to call first on a busy morning
Separating people you are still talking to from those who are settled
Giving the whole team the same shorthand
Filtering a long list down to the group that matters right now
Because search and filters understand status, you can pull up a particular group in moments, and even export them if you need a list elsewhere.
Keep your statuses few and meaningful.
A small set that everyone understands will do more for your team than a long list nobody remembers.

Behind every Harbour CRM account is a Client: the business that uses the product.
A small set of account settings keeps that Client's details accurate and your billing running smoothly.
Client name, which identifies your business in the account
Client contact number, so we and your team have a reliable phone number on file
Billing email, the address where billing messages are sent
Currency, which determines how monetary values such as Deal values are shown
These details change from time to time.
A business may rename, move to a new phone number, route billing to an accounts team, or begin trading in another currency.
Keeping the settings current avoids missed messages and confusion about figures.
They are kept deliberately simple, so account upkeep does not turn into an administrative project.
It is worth a quick review now and then, particularly after any change in your business.
Note that these settings relate to your business as the Client, not to your Contacts.

how to start using a CRM
Harbour CRM is designed to be useful from your first day.
You do not need a complicated rollout; a sensible start is enough.
A good way to begin is to think in layers:
Add your most important customers, with their phone numbers and email addresses
Link Contacts to Companies where it helps
Record your live Deals, and place them in the pipeline
Add custom fields for anything specific to your business
Check your account settings, including Client name, billing email and currency
Because Harbour CRM does not currently offer an import feature, many Clients begin by adding their most active Contacts first and building the list as they work.
It is a natural way to keep the data fresh and relevant.
As your records grow, search, filters and statuses keep everything easy to find, and a CSV export of your Contacts is always available.
Take it at your own pace.
Small, consistent habits will serve you better than a big push once.

is Harbour CRM right for my business
Harbour CRM suits businesses that want to look after their customers well without wrestling with heavy software.
If you keep your customers in a spreadsheet, an inbox or a notebook, and sense it is time for something more dependable, it was made with you in mind.
Sole traders and small teams who need one reliable list of Contacts
Service businesses that follow up with people over weeks or months
Sales-minded teams who want to see Deals moving through a pipeline
Businesses that deal with organisations and want Contacts linked to Companies
Owners who like to have their data within reach, with a CSV export of Contacts
It is a good fit when you value clarity over complexity: phone numbers and emails kept current, notes on every conversation, and a clear view of what is won, lost or still open.
If your needs are specialised, custom fields let you shape records around your own work.
Harbour CRM is not trying to be everything to everyone.
It aims to do the essentials well.

When a Client stores customer information in Harbour CRM, that information remains the Client's.
Your Contacts, Companies and Deals are your records, kept for your business to use.
There are a few principles worth knowing:
The Contacts you add, with their phone numbers, email addresses and notes, belong to you
Contacts can be exported as a CSV file at any time
Your account is managed by you.
Client details such as the Client name, Client contact number and billing email are kept in your account settings
Your customers' details deserve care, and you remain responsible for collecting and using them lawfully
We encourage every Client to record only what is useful, keep details accurate and remove what is no longer needed.
This page is a friendly overview rather than a legal document.
For the formal terms, please read our privacy policy and terms of service.

Harbour CRM is one member of a family of business tools.
The sister products are Harbour Invoicing, Harbour Mail, Harbour Desk, Harbour People and Harbour Projects, each designed to look after a different part of running a business.
Harbour Invoicing is for billing and getting paid
Harbour Desk is for customer support
Harbour People is for looking after your team
Harbour Projects is for organising work
Harbour CRM focuses on the relationship side: Contacts, Companies, Deals and the pipeline.
Many Clients find that this sits comfortably beside whichever other Harbour products they choose to use.
You do not need any other product to get full value from Harbour CRM.
It stands on its own, and you can add others when your business calls for them.
This page describes the family at a high level.
